hits.name: Naval
hits.text: When you look back, you’ll wish you’d just done the long-term version of everything.
hits.full_text: When you look back, you’ll wish you’d just done the long-term version of everything.
hits.draft_en:
I keep catching myself optimizing for the week that looks busy.

What I actually want is the long-term version: the same pen, the same plain page, showing up again tomorrow.

Not a bigger plan. Just the slow thing that still works in a year.
hits.video_tip: 20–30s: calendar/tabs in frame → close them → open one notebook → write tomorrow's one line. VO: 'The long-term version isn't a bigger plan. It's the slow thing that still works in a year.'

hits.name: Dan Koe
hits.text:
There are 3 things you can sell:

1) Your time, capped at 24 hours
2) Your things, capped by inventory
3) Your mind, for all of history, capped by how many rooms you could be in

Social media changed that completely. A brain and an internet connection can change your life.
hits.full_text:
There are 3 things you can sell:

2) Your things, capped by inventory

hits.hook: thedankoe — three things you can sell
hits.draft_en:
I'm not trying to sell every hour of my day.

I'm trying to put something honest on the page — something that can sit in someone else's hands when I'm not in the room.

A notebook. A quiet system. A line that still makes sense next year.

That's the kind of scale that feels like mine.
hits.video_tip: 25s desk: close laptop → open notebook → one line in favorite pen. VO: 'I'm not selling every hour. Just something honest that can sit in someone else's hands.'

hits.name: Sahil Bloom
hits.text: Simple thing that improved my life: I often choose the slower option on purpose. Walk instead of driving. Stairs instead of escalator. Cook instead of ordering. Whatever. In a world that wants you to rush, the ultimate act of rebellion is slowing down. There’s a power in that.
hits.full_text: Simple thing that improved my life: I often choose the slower option on purpose. Walk instead of driving. Stairs instead of escalator. Cook instead of ordering. Whatever. In a world that wants you to rush, the ultimate act of rebellion is slowing down. There’s a power in that.
hits.draft_en:
I often choose the slower option on purpose.

Write by hand instead of typing. One page instead of ten tabs. Sit with the unfinished thing instead of ordering a new plan.

Nothing dramatic. Just refusing to rush the part that needs quiet.
hits.video_tip: 20–30s: hand reaches for phone → sets it face-down → uncaps fountain pen → writes one slow line. VO: 'Choose the slower option on purpose.'
